subject: womens-health
title: Miscarriage and abortion care: key decisions for the exam

steps.tx: Miscarriage is loss of a pregnancy before 24 weeks. A **missed miscarriage** has no fetal cardiac activity but the tissue remains in the uterus. An **incomplete miscarriage** means some products are retained. Know which category the patient falls into before choosing management, because the options differ.
steps.say: Miscarriage is loss of a pregnancy before twenty four weeks. A missed miscarriage has no fetal cardiac activity but the tissue remains in the uterus. An incomplete miscarriage means some products are retained. Know which category the patient falls into before choosing management, because the options differ.

steps.tx: **Mifepristone** is an antiprogestogen. It blocks progesterone receptors in the decidua, which softens the cervix and sensitises the myometrium. **Misoprostol**, a prostaglandin analogue, then causes uterine contractions and expulsion. Medical abortion needs a confirmed intrauterine pregnancy of known gestation, so ultrasound confirmation comes first.

steps.tx: Ectopic pregnancy must be excluded before any termination or miscarriage plan. Unilateral pain, light bleeding, an empty uterus, an adnexal mass and free pelvic fluid suggest rupture. Haemodynamic stability does not exclude intraperitoneal bleeding, so **urgent gynaecological review** for surgery is required. Methotrexate is for selected stable cases only.

steps.tx: The scan shows an **empty uterus** beside a complex **adnexal mass** with dark **free pelvic fluid** pooling below. This triad points to ectopic pregnancy, possibly ruptured, rather than simple miscarriage. The lesson demands exclusion of ectopic before any evacuation plan, with urgent gynaecological review for surgery, since even a stable appearance cannot rule out bleeding inside.
steps.say: Always rule out ectopic pregnancy before any miscarriage or termination plan. Here the uterus is empty while an adnexal mass sits alongside free pelvic fluid, the classic ruptured pattern. Pain on one side with light bleeding should raise the same alarm. Stability does not exclude bleeding inside, so urgent gynaecological review for surgery is required. Learn this scan trio so evacuation never precedes exclusion.

vis.alt: The pelvic scan shows an empty uterus with an adnexal mass and free pelvic fluid.
vis.caption: Ectopic pattern with empty uterus plus fluid needing urgent review, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Sepsis after miscarriage or abortion is an emergency. Fever, tachycardia, raised white cell count, raised lactate and an open cervix with visible products suggest septic incomplete miscarriage. Start **IV broad-spectrum antibiotics** and arrange urgent uterine evacuation to remove the infected source. Take blood cultures first, but do not delay antibiotics.
